### Steps to reproduce
I haven't tried reproducing (for obvious reasons) but here's what I was doing when it happened:
- I had a Rust project with the following workspace (simplified):
```
project/Cargo.toml
project/src/main.rs
project/subcrate/
project/subcrate/Cargo.toml
project/subcrate/src/lib.rs
```
- From my file browser, I created `project/subcrate/examples/` and `project/subcrate/examples/example.rs`
- I opened the source for the example in nvim, already having some files from the workspace open, and rust-analyzer (with nvim LSP) said that the example file was not in the module path or something like that
- Upon hearing this, I tried to close and reopen nvim so it would recognize the module, but the RAM started ballooning like a forkbomb and it eventually got killed automatically

This might be a bug with rust-analyzer, or maybe even nvim-qt (though probably not, as nvim-qt did not end up crashing, but had a message saying `The Neovim process has crashed`)
Sorry it's not a very good report, but a very bad bug nonetheless
